title: Sean Hogan’s ‘The Dark Gets In’ Boarded for Worldwide Sales by Blue Finch Films Ahead of Beyond Fest Bow (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Blue Finch Films has boarded worldwide sales rights to “The Dark Gets In,” a supernatural thriller directed by Sean Hogan that will premiere at Beyo
body:
Blue Finch Films has boarded worldwide sales rights to “The Dark Gets In,” a supernatural thriller directed by Sean Hogan that will premiere at Beyond Fest later this month.

	The story centers on a documentary crew investigating a young girl’s disappearance, only to find themselves drawn into events far darker and stranger than they anticipated. Hogan builds the film around audiences’ fascination with the true crime documentary format before steering the narrative into unexpected supernatural territory.
	

	Hogan, known for “The Devil’s Business,” also wrote the screenplay. Evrim Ersoy, whose credits include “In a Cold Vein,” produced. Paul Goodwin, Nick Harwood, Jim Hinson, Mike Chapman and Fatima Hayward served as executive producers.


	In a statement, Hogan said: “‘The Dark Gets In’ is based upon an idea I had several years ago, but it wasn’t until I hit upon the notion of telling it in a true crime mockumentary format that it finally found its proper expression. We set out to make a film that initially felt very real and disturbing, but would eventually reveal itself to be something far more horrifying than the sort of story you typically see in such documentaries. The end result is, I hope, a mixture of tragedy and tension and slow-burning dread, and I’m excited to see how audiences respond to its many shocks and surprises.”

	Ersoy, who also produced “To Fire You Come At Last” with Hogan, added: “After the success of ‘To Fire You Come At Last,’ another opportunity to work with Sean was only natural – and with ‘The Dark Gets In,’ he has crafted a singularly unique film that delivers on the promise of its eerie atmosphere and will hopefully scare audiences around the world with its unique blend of the supernatural and true crime.”
	

	Blue Finch Films’ sales slate also includes Toronto Midnight Madness title “Kick On,” Fantastic Fest selected sci-fi horror-comedy “Flapjax,” and BBC Film and Screen Scotland-backed “Misson,” starring George MacKay.

title: Bestselling Japanese Novelist Maha Harada Says ‘If This Is a Dream, I Hope I Never Wake Up’ About Her San Sebastian – and Busan – Bound Directing Debut ‘In My Father’s Room’
description:

	Now 64, the best-selling Japanese author is makin
body:
Maha Harada spent two decades building scenes on the page before she ever stood behind a camera.

	Now 64, the best-selling Japanese author is making her feature directorial debut with “In My Father’s Room,” a film adapted from her own short story “An Unnecessary Man,” and it arrives in competition at the San Sebastian Film Festival before moving on to the Busan International Film Festival. 


	Ahead of both stops, Bitters End has already sold the film to France, Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong, with more territories under discussion.
	

	The transition from novels to film feels less like a leap than a continuation, Harada says. Her years working as a museum curator shaped how she writes long before she considered directing. “When I write fiction, I tend to depict scenes and the characters’ inner lives as if looking through a camera,” she says, adding that adapting “An Unnecessary Man” felt natural because the story is set in a town she once lived in and can still picture in exact detail. She describes the short story as an ordinary, universal story of a father and daughter, deliberately free of mysteries, schemes or sensual drama.


	That story follows Satomi, an art museum worker who learns almost nothing about her father, Yuichi, until after he has died alone. Harada says the character grew directly out of her own family. Her father sold art books, loved film and gambling, and “never stopped causing trouble,” she says, but he also introduced her to Picasso at age 10 and took her to see “Gone with the Wind” and “The Castle of Sand” at 12. It was only once he was gone, she says, that she understood how much he had taught her.
	

	Central to the film is the idea that Yuichi’s value cannot be measured by his usefulness to society, a theme Harada says she wanted to explore directly. “Whether or not you’re happy is something you decide for yourself,” she says, arguing that a life spent pursuing things whose worth is apparent only to oneself can still be a happy one, however little it resembles society’s idea of success. She adds that Yuichi’s willingness to die alone, having chased only what mattered to him, could be seen as extreme, but says no one can call his life anything other than happy.

	Visually, Harada built the film around two anchors: the Japanese tea ceremony, or chanoyu, and a painting by Mark Rothko. She wanted to bring the ceremony’s quiet, everyday symbolism to the screen, and to pair it with Rothko’s work as a Western counterpart to that same sense of beauty. She notes that Japanese museums collectively hold 10 works by Rothko, acquired by curators who recognized the artist’s spiritual quality decades before his prices climbed, a fact that still makes her proud.

	Moving from prose to a film set meant giving up some control, Harada says. Before filming began, she recalls, her assistant director read the script and asked her, “Isn’t there too much stage direction?” The comment made her realize that a novel is, in her words, almost entirely stage direction, with the writer controlling every detail the reader sees. On a film set, other collaborators have to be given room to interpret. She trimmed the script accordingly, and after being told there was “still too much explanation,” cut it further on set, ultimately paring the dialogue down to very little.

	Working with Yu Aoi, who plays Satomi, and Issey Ogata, who plays her father, Yuichi, reinforced that shift. She singles out a scene where Satomi comes home after being laid off and simply leaves the tap running, calling it a moment where Aoi conveyed despair through almost nothing at all, and says she sometimes forgot to call “cut” while watching her work. Ogata, she says, gave Yuichi a lived-in warmth, playing a father with no money or status who never lets go of the things he cares about most. She calls his performance of the tea ceremony one of the film’s biggest highlights.

	Cinematographer Yoshio Kitagawa, whose earlier credits include “Evil Does Not Exist,” shaped the film’s look alongside Harada during visits to tea ceremonies and museum viewings of Rothko’s work. She points to Yasujiro Ozu and Victor Erice’s “The Spirit of the Beehive” as touchstones for the film’s tone, and to Kei Kumai’s “Death of a Tea Master” as a specific visual reference for the ceremony scenes.
	

	Harada says reaching audiences outside Japan has been the hardest part of her writing career, even as her novels have found readers in South Korea, China and Taiwan. Entering the film world at 64 was partly about proving that age should not limit what someone takes on, she says, crediting the cast and crew who stayed with the project throughout.

	Having adapted and directed her own writing once, Harada says she is open to doing so again, though the idea of writing something built specifically for the screen, rather than adapting an existing novel, had not seriously occurred to her before now. She calls the process of directing “In My Father’s Room” a dreamlike experience unlike anything else in her career. “If this is a dream, I hope I never wake up,” she says. Asked what comes next, she says she plans to keep writing novels alongside directing more films, rather than choosing one path over the other, adding that doing both will make things twice as hard, and, she believes, twice as wonderful.

schema.headline: Bestselling Japanese Novelist Maha Harada Says ‘If This Is a Dream, I Hope I Never Wake Up’ About Her San Sebastian – and Busan – Bound Directing Debut ‘In My Father’s Room’

title: Latido Takes Isaki Lacuesta’s ‘Flamenco Sketches,’ San Sebastian’s Zabaltegi-Tabakalera Closer (EXCLUSIVE)
description: SAN SEBASTIAN, Spain – Madrid-based Latido Films has picked up international sales rights to Isaki Lacuesta’s “Flamenco Sketches” (“Jaleos”), the la
body:
SAN SEBASTIAN, Spain – Madrid-based Latido Films has picked up international sales rights to Isaki Lacuesta’s “Flamenco Sketches” (“Jaleos”), the latest film from Isaki Lacuesta, one of Spain’s most singular filmmakers, which plays this week at the San Sebastian Film Festival.

	Lacuesta has twice won San Sebastian’s top prize, the Golden Shell, with “The Double Steps” and “Between Two Waters.”


	“Flamenco Sketches” will close San Sebastian’s Zabaltegi-Tabakalera section. Using a vast array of archive footage, the film takes a freewheeling journey through the history of flamenco.
	

	“Isaki Lacuesta is without any doubt one of Spain’s most creative and innovative directors,” said Latido president Antonio Saura. “With ‘Flamenco Sketches’ he takes us on an unrivalled road of discovery of art, perception and joy.”

	Rather than offering a conventional history, the director builds the film as something closer to flamenco itself: stories begin, mutate, collide and disappear; images, music and ideas summon themselves intuitively.

	The film jumps from flamenco’s first appearances in the mid-19th century to the arrival of trains, clocks and standardized time; from Thomas Edison’s early moving images of Spanish dancer Carmencita to the relationship between flamenco and the artistic avant-garde; from Vicente Escudero and Man Ray to Francis Picabia, Joan Miró and Marcel Duchamp.

	The project has been years in the making. Speaking to Variety in 2024, Lacuesta described it as “a kind of ‘One Thousand and One Nights,’ a story that explains tales, tales of flamenco.”
	

	“What do Edison, Hitler, Leni Riefenstahl, Tarantino and Camarón de la Isla all have in common?” he said. “They all have stories that have to do with flamenco. Flamenco has always been modern and attached to modern history.”

	Lacuesta and his co-writers Pedro G. Romero and Luis Parés also probe what happens when an spontaneous, living form is recorded and ‘preserved.’ The film continually circles the paradox of the art form surviving through mutation and contradiction, even as attempts are made to establish what constitutes “real” flamenco.

	Its cast of voices includes figures from flamenco, and the arts more broadly including rapper C. Tangana, director of the memorable “La guitarra flamenca de Yerai Cortés,” dancer Rocío Molina, artist Pedro G. Romero and french philosopher and art historian Georges Didi-Huberman.

	“Flamenco Sketches” is produced by Tono Folguera for Lastor Media and Guillermo Cascante for Goroka Contents, with Lacuesta’s La Termita Films as co-producer. BTeam Pictures handles Spanish distribution, with Latido selling worldwide outside Spain.

	The title echoes Miles Davis’ “Flamenco Sketches,” but Lacuesta’s own sketchbook, like the jazz great, revels in contradiction.

schema.headline: Latido Takes Isaki Lacuesta’s ‘Flamenco Sketches,’ San Sebastian’s Zabaltegi-Tabakalera Closer (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Tobias Forge’s ‘V/H/S Mixtape’ Segment, Swedish Horror ‘Trespassers,’ ‘The End’ by ‘Midsommar’ Production Designer on Mylla Films Slate (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Swedish boutique genre specialist Mylla Films, brainchild of “Midsommar” producer Patrik Andersson and Nordic indie distribution heavyweight Jakob A
body:
Swedish boutique genre specialist Mylla Films, brainchild of “Midsommar” producer Patrik Andersson and Nordic indie distribution heavyweight Jakob Abrahamsson (CEO of NonStop Entertainment), has turned into a magnet for Nordic genre talent since its splashy launch in Cannes in 2022.

	“People with tremendous CVs and filmographies are reaching out to us,” Abrahamsson told Variety on the eve of the Helsinki Film Festival industry confab Finnish Film Affair, where Mylla Films’ project “Trespassers” (“Inkräktare”) will be pitched to potential co-financiers.
	



	

					“Trespassers” concept art
									Courtesy of Mylla Films
	



	The latest Swedish star name added to Mylla Films’ roster is musician Tobias Forge, frontman of Grammy-winning theatrical metal act Ghost — the first hard rock band to top album charts in four years with “Skeletá” in 2025. Forge will make his directorial debut with the music video segment of U.S.-fully financed “V/H/S/ Mixtape,” latest instalment in the horror anthology franchise, which will world premiere at L.A.’s Beyond Fest on Sept. 30, ahead of its Shudder launch on Oct. 9.


	The five minutes and a half clip, starring Gustav Hammarsten (“Brüno,” “The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo”) and Nour el-Refai (“Jordskott,” “The Bonus Family”), is “an old school story-driven death metal music video,” said the versatile Andersson, himself a seasoned musician.



	

					“The End”
									Courtesy of Mylla Films
	



	“We were contacted in June and managed to turn around Tobias’ segment in three months. It’s been extremely fun and frankly astonishing!” said Abrahamsson, who will release “V/H/S/ Mixtape” in the Nordics via NonStop Entertainment.
	

	Another of Mylla Films’ recent recruits is Henrik Svensson, production designer of Ari Aster’s “Midsommar” and Kristoffer Borgli’s “Sick of Myself,” now making his directorial debut with the low budget “The End.”

	“The End,” which is fully-financed by private equity coin and stars prolific Swedish author Mattias Ribbing, is described by Andersson as “an avant-garde experimental audiovisual film featuring literally killing soundtracks,” with stunts designed by “Kung Fury’s” Eos Karlsson. “We’ve tried to do a Jodorowsky film in Sweden, which has been lots of fun. We can’t wait to showcase it,” said Andersson, who’s eying a genre festival launchpad in the spring 2027.

	While “The End” and Forge’s “V/H/S/ Mixtape” segment are prime examples of Mylla’s core objective, which is “to fertilize the soil of genre filmmaking in the Nordics,” the innovative and lower cost turnaround jobs have also been a response to the tough film financing conditions that have forced Mylla’s founders to slightly readjust their initial plans.

	While “Bloodsuckers,” Mylla’s first fiction feature length is set to hit screens early 2027 via NonStop Entertaiment, with Charades handling sales, higher-end projects such as Michael Marcimain’s gothic western “Devastation” have been slower to take off. “We were super ambitious when we set off, but projects need to make sense [financially]; everything takes time today, therefore we’re a bit more agile in terms of scope,” acknowledged Abrahamsson.

	“We have a [theatrical] market in Sweden that no one is really relying on at the moment, and it’s super hard to get people to accept the risk analysis of your projects,” added Andersson. “That said, we have clear visions and although we’re very much part of the Swedish system, we know how to navigate the international market.”

	Trespassers Watch OutWhen “Trespassers” is pitched for the first time on Thursday at Finnish Film Affair, Mylla Films will be seeking to woo partners looking for a quality jump scare anchored in Nordic folk.

	First on board the €3 million ($3.4 million) project is Scandi distribution group Scanbox. “They are very enthusiastic about it and stepped on board early on and have been helping us develop the script,” said Andersson.
	

	“Trespassers” is Johannes Persson’s sophomore feature film, following horror movie “Feed” – which bagged an audience prize at Sweden’s national Guldbagge film awards in 2023. It is co-penned with Melina Maraki, the writer behind SVT’s hit show “Summer of 1985.”

	“One night, I was looking out the window of an old, run-down house. A group dragged a man into the yard, stripped him, bound his legs, and hoisted him upside down. As one of them raised an ax ready to cleave him in two, I awoke. That morning, I began writing in both directions, from before and after the nightmare. That’s how ‘Trespassers’ was born,” Persson told Variety.

	“The story turns on four young people from a failed anti-establishment movement, who travel to the vast wilderness of Northern Sweden to reconnect with nature. But after a river rafting accident leaves them stranded, they discover they are not alone — and not welcome — on land controlled by a group that has isolated itself for centuries with its own terrifying beliefs,” reads the synopsis.

	“’Deliverance’ is a close inspiration, with big city guys trying to connect with nature and — wrongly —expecting it to be welcoming and good. This premise is what attracted us to ‘Trespassers,’” said Abrahamsson.

	Persson, who boasts an impressive track record as casting director of more than 30 Swedish productions such as “A Man Called Ove,” “Borg vs McEnroe,” the Netflix series “Snabba Cash” and “The Conference,” is already assembling an A-list cast.

	Shooting is set to start late summer 2027.

	At this week’s Finnish Film Affair and workshop Nordic Genre Lab, Mylla Films’ partners said they “look forward to having international eyes on the set-up, premise, characters and pacing of this piece of dynamite.”

schema.headline: Tobias Forge’s ‘V/H/S Mixtape’ Segment, Swedish Horror ‘Trespassers,’ ‘The End’ by ‘Midsommar’ Production Designer on Mylla Films Slate (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Karan Johar’s Dharma Productions Confirms Film on Indian Spymaster Rameshwar Nath Kao, Targets 2028 Release (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Karan Johar‘s Dharma Productions is teaming with Leo Media Collective on a theatrical feature about Rameshwar Nath Kao, founder of India’s Research
body:
Karan Johar‘s Dharma Productions is teaming with Leo Media Collective on a theatrical feature about Rameshwar Nath Kao, founder of India’s Research and Analysis Wing, targeting an Aug. 11, 2028 release timed to the Indian Independence Day holiday weekend.

	R&AW, India’s primary external intelligence agency, was established in 1968 to consolidate the country’s foreign intelligence operations, which had previously been handled by the Intelligence Bureau.
	

	The untitled film is currently in development. The announcement was made on Sept. 21, marking 58 years since R&AW’s founding, with the makers eyeing the 2028 release date to coincide with the agency’s 60th anniversary. The project was initially announced in early 2020. 


	“Leo media has painstakingly been researching and dramatising this narrative with passion for the past two years, we want this film to be a gripping story based on true facts to pay homage to R&AW and honour their milestone year with a solid motion picture … all of us at Dharma are so excited to get going,” Johar said.

	The espionage actioner is based on Nitin Gokhale’s book “Gentleman Spymaster,” with production slated to begin by mid-2026. Casting, director and other key details have not been disclosed, though an as yet unnamed A-list actor is attached to lead the project.

	The story spans 1955 to 1971, tracing the lead-up to R&AW’s formation and its first mission during the 1971 war against Pakistan. Kao is widely regarded within Indian intelligence circles as a formative figure in the country’s espionage apparatus, with successive R&AW chiefs having credited his strategic approach.
	

	The project marks a reunion between Dharma Productions and Leo Media Collective following “Bad Newz” (2024) and “Kesari: Chapter 2” (2025). It also continues Dharma’s run of films drawn from real events and figures, including “Kesari,” “Raazi” and “Shershaah.”

schema.headline: Karan Johar’s Dharma Productions Confirms Film on Indian Spymaster Rameshwar Nath Kao, Targets 2028 Release (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Chile Film Industry Surges 20.5% Compared to Previous Season, New Catalog Reveals (EXCLUSIVE)
description: CinemaChile unveils its 2026-2027 catalog at the San Sebastián Festival on Sept. 21 where it has much to celebrate, with eight titles screening acro
body:
CinemaChile unveils its 2026-2027 catalog at the San Sebastián Festival on Sept. 21 where it has much to celebrate, with eight titles screening across seven sections, led by Pablo Larrain’s “My Sad Dead,” a 4-part Netflix series that has been combined to make a roughly three-hour feature that competes for the Golden Shell.

	Unsurprisingly, the catalog proves that this tiny county of some 20 million inhabitants continues to punch above its weight, with the catalog reporting a 20.5% growth in Chile’s film industry compared with the 2025-2026 period.
	

	Said Gabriela Sandoval, a CinemaChile board member: “We have gone from 156 to 188 titles, which is clearly great news and demonstrates the strength of Chilean cinema, which has continued to grow over the past five years.” In 2021, Chile reported 139 titles.


	Sandoval notes that the latest figures bring further positive developments: Of the 188 films, 66 are directed or co-directed by women, while 100 are productions or co-productions featuring leading industry professionals.

	“The work of female directors and producers is not only growing, but their films are also shining around the world,” she said, pointing to the Chilean filmmakers and producers attending this year’s San Sebastián Festival.

	Also notable is that more than 80% of the titles are international co-productions, linking Chile with 23 countries, including Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Spain, France, Italy, Germany, the U.K., the U.S., South Korea, Switzerland, the Netherlands and Qatar.

	Given the country’s size, this is to be expected. As Pablo Larrain’s producing partner and brother Juan de Dios Larraín pointed out at a talk held at the Guadalajara Film Festival in April, it was precisely the size of Chile’s market that has forced them and their peers to look outward in order to make their films.
	

	“Co-production isn’t just helpful—it’s essential to Chilean cinema. There’s really no other way to do it. You can’t finance a film purely through the Chilean market; the numbers just don’t add up. So, from early on, going out and seeking funding became a fundamental part of the process – it’s built into the system,” he said.

	“In a way, that limitation forces growth. It pushes you to adapt, collaborate and think beyond your own borders from the very beginning,” he added.

	Noted Sandoval: “The catalogue is a snapshot of an increasingly diverse, internationalized and connected sector, where new voices coexist with established filmmakers.”

	“Beyond the growing number of titles, the 188 films offer a clear picture of the Chilean audiovisual sector today: active, diverse and deeply connected to the world.”

	She added: “San Sebastián is especially significant for presenting the catalogue because that same picture is reflected in the Festival’s programming. Chilean cinema appears across sections, formats and generations, from Official Selection to New Directors, Horizontes Latinos, Perlak, Zabaltegi, Made in Spain and Zinemira. This breadth reflects what CinemaChile wants to show: there is no single way to define Chilean cinema today.”

	Aside from Larrain’s film in main competition, New Directors features Thomas Woodroffe’s debut “Erratics” (“Bloques erráticos”) vies for the main prize in the festival’s New Directors compeition and Horizontes Latinos includes two films by established female directors, Manuela Martelli’s “The Meltdown” (El deshielo”) and Dominga Sotomayor’s “The Dog” (“La perra”).

	Zabaltegi features Felipe Luis’ Cannes-winning short “For the Opponents” (“Para los contrincantes”) while Perlak presents John Malkovich-led “Wild Horse Nine,” shot on Easter Island and starring Chilean actresses Mariana di Girolamo and Paola Giannini.

	Made in Spain screens “This Body of Mine” (Este cuerpo mío”) by Chilean-born director Afioco Gnecco, partly shot in Chile. Zinemira features the animated feature “Winnipeg, the Seed of Hope” (“Winnipeg, el barco de la esperanza”).

schema.headline: Chile Film Industry Surges 20.5% Compared to Previous Season, New Catalog Reveals (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Korea Box Office: Local Comedy Remake ‘The Intern’ Leads Weekend Admissions as ‘The Odyssey’ Retains Revenue Crown
description: South Korean comedy-drama remake “The Intern” debuted atop the local box office in ticket admissions during the weekend of Sept. 18–20, though Chris
body:
South Korean comedy-drama remake “The Intern” debuted atop the local box office in ticket admissions during the weekend of Sept. 18–20, though Christopher Nolan’s holdover epic “The Odyssey” continued to lead overall weekend revenue, generating a higher gross.

	According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the newly released local title generated $1.9 million from a chart-topping 275,183 admissions over the three-day frame across 1,428 screens to claim 26% of the weekend market. By comparison, “The Odyssey” generated a weekend-high $2.3 million but finished second on the official admissions chart with 256,789 tickets across 1,253 screens, taking 30.7% of total box office revenue.
	

	Directed by Kim Do-young, the Warner Bros. Korea adaptation of Nancy Meyers’ 2015 Hollywood comedy stars Choi Min-sik and Han So-hee. The narrative follows a 70-year-old retired executive with 37 years of corporate experience who re-enters the workforce as a senior intern at a high-velocity fashion startup run by a driven young CEO. Since launching wide on Sept. 16, the feel-good release has drawn 403,903 total admissions for an overall cumulative gross of $2.8 million. 


	“The Odyssey” saw its local gross climb to $91.1 million from 11,217,639 total ticket buyers since its Aug. 5 launch. 

	“Obsession” held third place in its third weekend, earning $1 million from 131,467 admissions across 762 screens. The film accounted for 13.6% of the frame, lifting its cume to $5.4 million from 701,713 viewers since its Sept. 2 rollout.

	“Resident Evil” opened in fourth place, pulling in $623,228 from 80,779 admissions across 679 screens. Since its Sept. 17 premiere, the horror title has accumulated $783,336 from 103,654 viewers.
	

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” placed fifth in its eighth weekend of release, taking $214,082 from 33,636 admissions across 540 screens. The film accounted for 2.8% of the frame, bringing its gross to $67.1 million. 

	Anime feature “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” landed in sixth place ahead of its wide release, generating $199,794 from 20,734 admissions across preview screenings. Directed by Kei Oikawa and based on the manga series by Nagano, the fantasy adventure follows Chiikawa and companions traveling to an island paradise before uncovering an ominous threat. The film has grossed $202,845 from 21,203 admissions ahead of its Sept. 30 rollout.

	Mamoru Hosoda’s 2006 anime classic “The Girl Who Leapt Through Time” took seventh place via a 20th-anniversary theatrical re-release, earning $97,270 from 12,153 admissions across 150 screens for an updated cume of $736,815 from 132,656 tickets.

	Double-feature anime re-release “Digimon Adventure & Digimon Adventure: Our War Game!” opened in eighth place, pulling in $89,411 from 11,456 admissions across 205 screens since its Sept. 16 bow, reaching a cumulative total of $138,143 from 17,764 admissions.

	“The Drama” finished in ninth place with $75,165 from 9,527 admissions, lifting its gross to $583,238 from 80,094 total viewers.

	Rounding out the top 10 was gambling crime thriller “Tazza: The Song of Beelzebub,” which took $60,860 from 6,999 admissions across festival and special previews. Directed by Choi Kook-hee and starring Byun Yo-han, Noh Jae-won, and Ayaka Miyoshi, the fourth instalment in the franchise, which centers on high-stakes competitive Texas hold’em and international casino circuits, accumulated $147,019 from 19,183 viewers ahead of its wide release on Sept. 23.

schema.headline: Korea Box Office: Local Comedy Remake ‘The Intern’ Leads Weekend Admissions as ‘The Odyssey’ Retains Revenue Crown

title: Secuoya Studios Taps Carla Gómez to Lead Latin American Development as Regional Expansion Accelerates (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Spain’s Secuoya Studios has tapped Carla Gómez as head of development and executive producer for Latin America, strengthening its creative and produ
body:
Spain’s Secuoya Studios has tapped Carla Gómez as head of development and executive producer for Latin America, strengthening its creative and production operations in the region.

	Bringing more than two decades of experience in the television and streaming sector, Gómez will oversee the development of original projects from initial concept through production. She also brings a catalogue of intellectual property and projects developed through her boutique development company, Cielito Studio.
	

	Her appointment follows Secuoya’s announcement in April that it was granting its Latin American operation greater autonomy over development, production and greenlight decisions, targeting Mexico, Colombia and the U.S. Hispanic market.


	The regional business is headed by Daniel Hernández Bocanegra, managing director of Secuoya Studios in Latin America, with Pierluigi Gazzolo serving as a strategic adviser through Farniente Media.

	“Carla Gómez’s arrival marks an important step in the continued strengthening of both our team and our strategy in Latin America,” Hernández Bocanegra said. “We share the same commitment to working closely with local talent and stories to develop distinctive content capable of connecting with international audiences.” 

	Gómez has worked with content teams at ViX, HBO and Viacom, produced for NBCUniversal and, most recently, served as a development consultant for Netflix in Colombia.

	Her executive credits include ViX productions “Isla Brava,” “El Gallo de Oro,” “La Mujer del Diablo” and “María Félix: La Doña,” alongside HBO Latin America’s “Sierra Madre” and Nickelodeon’s “Grachi” and its U.S. adaptation, “Every Witch Way.”
	

	“I strongly believe in the ‘local for local’ vision: content created within the region, for our audiences and their cultures,” Gómez said.



	

									‘La celda de los milagros’ Courtesy of Secuoya Studios
	



	Secuoya’s regional production drive has already yielded Netflix hit “La Celda de los Milagros,” which topped the streamer’s global non-English-language film rankings for the week of Feb. 16-22. The film recorded 21 million worldwide views in the first half of 2026, according to Netflix.

	The studio’s Latin American slate also includes the upcoming “Belleza,” produced with BH5 for Miércoles Entertainment, and “La Corona,” a collaboration with Black Sheep Productions, Startling, Infinity Hill and Runaway Films.

schema.headline: Secuoya Studios Taps Carla Gómez to Lead Latin American Development as Regional Expansion Accelerates (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Spanish Government Pledges to Continue Audiovisual Hub Through Spain Crece Fund
description: Spain plans to press on with its commitment to the country’s  audiovisual industry, said Óscar López, Minister for Digital Transformation and Public
body:
Spain plans to press on with its commitment to the country’s  audiovisual industry, said Óscar López, Minister for Digital Transformation and Public Administration. Speaking at the conference titled The New Script of the Audiovisual Industry at the San Sebastian Festival, López said Sunday that his Ministry would continue supporting its audiovisual industry through the Spain Crece Fund.

	That looks likely to feature further strategic investment via SETT, the Ministry’s sovereign venture capital fund. 
	

	“When a public policy works, it should be maintained without a deadline. It is the golden age for our audiovisual sector,” he said, pointing to a series of record-breaking figures.


	López spoke just hours before “La Bola Negra,” from Spain’s Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, won the 2026 TIFF People’s Choice Award, a coveted audience prize at the annual film festival in Toronto. which, according to Variety, is largely seen as an indicator of legs on the road to the Oscars stage.

	Four Spanish series seasons and three movies feature in Netflix Top 10s of the streaming giant’s biggest non-English hits ever, more titles than from any other country in the world.  

	“We had the talent, the ideas and the locations. What was missing was political will and a significant injection of capital,” López continued. He pointed to the Spain Audiovisual Hub Plan as a key driver of the sector’s development, describing it as “an unprecedented institutional commitment commensurate with the scale of the challenge” that made it possible “to design an economic transformation on an unprecedented scale.”
	

	“And here we are, €1.6 billion later, reaping the benefits and expanding our horizons,” he said.

	Statistics Reveal Spain’s Dramatic Growth

	Spain is now the European Union’s largest production market, while audiovisual production in the country grew by 31% in 2025. Spanish productions also account for nine of the 11 most-watched series in Europe, according to the figures cited by the minister.

	Employment in the sector has doubled since 2020, rising from 30,900 workers to more than 64,000 in 2025.

	López noted that “the industry will soon benefit from the €450 million in investments mobilized by SETT (Spanish Society for Technological Transformation), in companies such as Lazona, Good Films and Aurora Media.”

	High Praise for SETT, the Venture Capital Fund of Spain’s Ministry for Digital Transformation

	Speaking at the first of three panels, Good Film Studios founder Miriam Segal praised Spain’s studios, talent and international potential. Having worked across the U.S., UK and Europe, she said she “didn’t know about this incredible” industry infrastructure or the government’s “extraordinary passion and commitment” to the sector. For the first time as an independent producer, this support has enabled her to offer pay-or-play deals to actors. Ánima Kitchen’s José Carlos Garcia thanked SETT for supporting the company’s vision, enabling growth, talent recruitment and plans for three high-end animated films in five years, adding that SETT would help expand Ánima’s animation leadership.

	Europe Panel: A Roadmap to the Future

	The panel brought together perspectives from Spain, Greece and Denmark on how Europe can remain culturally diverse while competing globally. They agreed there is no single European audiovisual model, with Carla Redondo of Spain’s Ministry of Digital Transformation describing this diversity as “one of the true strengths” of Europe. Spain highlighted incentives, investment, talent and infrastructure, while Greece stressed using international productions to build local capacity and training. Esben Snoer Iversen Denmark’s Culture Ministry emphasized regional cooperation and flexible funding as the media landscape evolves. Speakers also called for greater administrative harmonization and support for emerging creative industries. As Leonidas Christopoulos of Ekkomed put it, “it’s all about the stories”: strong content ultimately drives international competitiveness.
	

	Linear Television is Not Dead

	The third panel explored how broadcasters and platforms are adapting to a rapidly changing audiovisual landscape. Said Mediaset’s Fernando Hernaiz” “Television is not dead” but has evolved into a broader “ecosystem” spanning linear channels, streaming, production and distribution. “We have a capacity to adapt,” he said, noting that television is now “technology, creation, scripts and business.” Audience fragmentation and measurement remain major challenges, while the panelists, including RTVE’s Alfonso Morales, Atresmedia’s Miguel Langle and Movistar Plus’ Clara Ruipérez called for regulation that keeps pace with platforms and social media. Investment, promotion and strong storytelling were seen as essential to making Spanish content travel internationally.

	Sneak Peek at the Olsberg-SP Data

	Spain Film Commission’s Juan Manuel Guimerans and Leon Forde of Olsberg SPI gave a sneak peek of the Olsberg study of the country’s audiovisual sector based on official data, which estimates €20 billion in direct production expenditure between 2020 and 2025, generating nearly €18 billion in gross value added and supporting around 64,000 jobs. Direct investment grew 45%, while gross value added rose 38%. More than half of employment generated by the sector comes through related industries and supply chains, including construction, hospitality and transport. Forde stressed that data is essential for effective policymaking but remains fragmented across the complex industry. They described audiovisual as an “ecosystem” where “all [species] are indispensable,” requiring continued investment and balance. A more detailed report will be presented on Sept.22. 

	John Hopewell contributed to this article.

title: Tatiana Huezo, Juan Sebastián Mesa, Mónica Lima, Val Jashari Among 10 Filmmakers Vying for WIP LatAm and Europa Awards at San Sebastián
description: A total of 10 projects are taking part in the San Sebastian Film Festival’s Latin America and Europe WIP competition showcases, which will help the
body:
A total of 10 projects are taking part in the San Sebastian Film Festival’s Latin America and Europe WIP competition showcases, which will help the winning projects jump their last hurdles towards release.   

	Selected from hundreds of submissions, six projects are vying for for the coveted WIP Latam Industry Award and four titles from across Europe are competing for the WIP Europa Industry Award. 


	The WIP Latam Industry Award covers the post-production of a film, a DCP subtitled in English and its distribution in Spain. Among the six contenders are the latest from Mexico’s Tatiana Huezo (“Prayers for the Stolen”), venturing into fiction again, and Juan Sebastián Mesa’s multi-country co-production, “Lovers Go Home!”
	

	Also in contention is the EGEDA Platino Industria Award of $34,466 (€30,000), which is handed to the lead producer of the winning film.

	“We received projects spanning a wide range of genres and approaches and this year we wanted the final selection to reflect that diversity. Alongside more traditional genres such as drama, comedy and road movies, we also received a number of more hybrid non-fiction projects,” said Javier Martin, selection committee member and Latin American delegate, who added that, as in previous editions, only 30% of the projects they received were directed by women filmmakers.

	“We were particularly interested in highlighting work from Mexico and Brazil, two countries currently experiencing a remarkable creative moment and that have made significant strides in terms of film production in recent years. Colombia is also worth highlighting, as its cinema is opening up to a new generation of particularly exciting filmmakers,” he told Variety.
	

	With regards to Argentine cinema, he said: “We continue to receive a significant number of outstanding projects. However, given the country’s current circumstances, many filmmakers have had to scale back their ambitions. Projects are increasingly being developed through more “collaborative” co-production models, while still requiring international partners to reach completion.”

	Since its creation in 2020, WIP Latam has enabled the completion of multiple selected films. Among the stand outs are: “If We Don’t Burn, How Do We Light Up the Night” by Kim Torres, selected for New Directors last year, Fernando Eimbcke’s “Flies,” which world premiered at the Berlinale, and Ecuador’s “Octopus Skin” by Ana Cristina Barragan.

	The WIP Latam Industry Award is granted by A Contracorriente Films, Best Digital, Deluxe Content Services Spain, Dolby, Laserfilm Cine y Vídeo, Nephilim Producciones and No Problem Sonido.

	WIP Latin America takes place Sept 21-23 at the festival, which runs Sept. 18-26.

	WIP LatAm Contenders:

	“Everywhere Left to Go” (“Todos los lugares donde ir,” Tiagx Vélez, Crisalida Cine, Colombia)

	When his boyfriend disappears during a techno rave, Miguel spirals into grief and an increasingly fractured reality, seeking connection among lovers, strangers and his mother’s partner. Ana Tiagx Vélez’s second feature follows her debut “The Origin of Species.” Her shorts include “We Will Be,” winner of the Dunkel Roda Award, “Omen,” selected for Ficunam and Cartagena Film Fest, and “The Third World After the Sun,” presented at Rotterdam.



	

					Everywhere Left to Go
	



	“Galerna” (Tatiana Huezo, Pimienta Films, Elastica Films, Mexico, Spain)

	Huezo’s latest film follows Lúa and Noé, casting directors searching remote Mexico for natural actors for a sci-fi production, where their journey challenges their prejudices and vulnerabilities. The project brings together prominent producers with credits including “Roma,” “Prayers for the Stolen” and “Sujo” (Pimiento) and “Alcarràs,” “Summer 1993,” “Creatura” and “Romería “(Elástica). Starring Ilse Salas (“The Good Girls”) and Ariel-nominated Lázaro Gabino Rodríguez (“Fauna”) with cinematography by Huezo’s long-time collaborator Ernesto Pardo.
	

	“Lovers Go Home!” (Juan Sebastián Mesa, Rhayuela Films, Potenza Prods., Camera Oscura, Dublin Films, El Sol Ermitaño, Colombia, Spain, Canada, France)

	Multi-country co-production shot in Canada and Colombia follows Alejandra, a single mother who works as a webcam performer in a Medellin studio, and her unlikely bond with disabled war veteran Andrew. The two begin a series of virtual conversations ranging from sexual requests to trivial challenges. Drama participated in the Euro-Latin Co-Production forum in 2022, Carolina Foundation Screenwriting Workshop, the Chalet Mauriac residency and Cinéma en Développement at the Toulouse Film Festival.



	

					Lovers Go Home
	



	“The Criminal Matter” (Matías Italo Scarvaci, Naso Cine, By LACE Films, Argentina, Chile)

	Debut fiction feature. Two brothers pursuing the American dream become entangled in a dangerous operation involving corruption, violence and the Russian mafia, while betrayal threatens their bond. Scarvaci’s first docu feature, “Docile Bodies” (2015), co-directed with Diego Gachassin, received a special mention at Mar del Plata, plus the DAC Best Director and Argentores awards. “Other Seed” (2022) competed in Guadalajara, while his latest “The Days with Her” (2025) screened in Moscow’s documentary competition.



	

					The Criminal Matter
	



	“The Last Song of The Birds” (“O ultimo canto dos pássaros,” Beatriz Seigner, Cine-Sud, Oportuna Films, Brazil, France, Uruguay)

	Drama follows Hugo, 14, who must find his estranged Uruguayan father to secure a passport and join his São Paulo orchestra on a European tour. Film is represented by Pyramide Intl, with cinematography by Inti Briones. Director Seigner previously made “Los silencios,” which premiered at Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight and won the Cooperación Española Award in San Sebastián, establishing her as an international festival presence. Participated in the 2022 Europe-Latin America Co-Production Forum.



	

					The Last Song of the Birds
	



	“Travel & Pleasure” (“Viajes y placeres,” Mariano Luque, Largavista Cine, Cabustra Arts, Animista Cine, Argentina, Uruguay)

	A fading TV presenter travels with a friend to Argentina’s Embalse lake to film a new episode of “Travel & Pleasure,” but discovers mysterious alien eggs and begins investigating their origins. Mariano Luque previously directed “Salsipuedes,” which premiered at San Sebastián and Cannes Cinéfondation, “Otra madre” at Rotterdam and “Los árboles” at Cinéma du Réel. “Travel & Pleasure” was selected for the 2022 Europe-Latin America Co-Production Forum with the working title “Inspection on Earth.”
	



	

					Travel & Pleasure
	



	The WIP Europa Industry Award likewise consists of post-production services, English and Spanish DCP subtitling and distribution in Spain.

	WIP Europa Contenders:

	“The Battle of Hedgehogs,” M. Tayfur Aydın(MTA Film Yapim, Turkey)

	Following the death of her father, Zerin opposes her brothers’ plan to divide and sell the family property, seeing it as the inheritance she has earned through years of sacrifice. Her resistance ignites a conflict that exposes hidden secrets, shifting loyalties and traditions that have shaped the family for generations. The film is described as “an intimate and emotionally charged family drama about justice, belonging, and the courage to challenge inherited rules.”



	

					The Battle of Hedgehogs
	



	“In a Manner of Speaking,” Val Jashari(Wavemaker Films, Live Productions, Kosovo, Montenegro)

	Zeka, an Albanian-American fugitive running a bar in Prishtina, suddenly sees her hidden life upended by a police raid. Cornered, Zeka leaps onto a balcony and meets Vlora, a woman from a remote village trying to disappear for reasons of her own. Both confined in a tight space and strangers to one another, they begin to face all that they have suppressed, setting off on an unexpected journey toward redemption.



	

					In a Manner of Speaking
	



	“The First Week of August,” Filip Mojzes(Wolfgang & Dolly, Black Photon,Croatia, Poland)

	While on summer vacation with his wife Ivana and 10-year-old son David, Zoran, a journalist who has experienced psychological trauma, unexpectedly and violently attacks the boy as he slowly begins to lose control over his behavior. As the vacation progresses, deeper issues in Zoran and Ivana’s relationship begin to surface, and these problems eventually extend to their interactions with a neighboring family.



	

					The First Week of August
	



	“Familiar Feelings,” Mónica Lima(Seara Filmes, Maria Zimbro, Portugal)

	Lia, once a promising actress, unexpectedly returns to her drought-stricken homeland in rural Portugal. While expecting an empty house, she finds her family gathered to receive her. Startled, she hides and slips away, postponing the confrontation. Amid a landscape marked by drought and decay, Lia drifts between distance and belonging until a fragile reunion forces them all to confront unfulfilled dreams, inherited fractures, and the desperate longing for connection.



	

					Familiar Feelings

title: Lionel Richie Seen For First Time After Hospitalization
description:
Lionel Richie
                          First Outing After Hospitalization
body:
Lionel Richie
                          First Outing After Hospitalization
                          Hello ... Is It Me You're Looking For?
                      
      
    
            Can't slow Lionel Richie down ... cuz he's out of the hospital!!!
      
    
            The 77-year-old singer stepped out saying 'Hello' to the fans while on the town with his girlfriend, Lisa Parigi, as they attended a party in Beverly Hills Saturday night ... and it seems like his recent hospitalization is merely a distant memory.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Looking sharp in a navy jacket with matching pants ... Lionel kept it casual with some white sneakers and a thumbs up to the camera.
      

            As TMZ first reported, the entertainer checked himself into the hospital on August 29 for testing.
      
    
            Lionel was on stage hours before he checked into the hospital. The singer appeared weak while at his concert and had to sit for a portion of the performance. 
      
    
            A source close to Lionel potential dehydration was the reason for his hospitalization, while other sources told us the issues were related to his heart. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            After a 3-day stay at a St. Louis hospital, Lionel got the all-clear from docs on September 2 and headed back to Los Angeles.
      
    
            Now, we've got eyes on Lionel ... and he's steppin' out on the town "All Night Long!"

title: ICE Shoots and Wounds Man in Austin

                          Man Shot and Wounded
body:
ICE in Austin
                          Man Shot and Wounded
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 20, 2026
                
                            3:37 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 20, 2026
                                5:08 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            ICE agents have shot and injured a man in Austin, Texas ... and investigators are being tight lipped about the altercation.
      
    
            Sunday afternoon, a man -- whose name, age, and race have not been revealed -- was shot, injured, and transported to a local hospital, this according to a press conference given by Austin officials.
      
    
            City officials made it clear that the Austin Police Department was not involved in the incident -- and Mayor Kirk Watson also emphasized that he is "not happy at all" about the fact that there was a shooting involving someone who "purports to be law enforcement."
      

            Mayor Watson said in the press conference that the victim was transferred to the hospital and remains in serious, but stable condition.
      
    
            A large police presence remains at the scene in North Austin where the shooting occurred.
      
    
            The Chief of Police Lisa Davis assured Austinites the police, EMS, and the mayor's office are all demanding answers about what occurred leading up to the shooting. EMS Chief Rob Luckritz said that although they were not on the scene at the time of the shooting, they arrived within three and a half minutes.
      
    
            Rep. Greg Casar spoke, saying "ICE has not been truthful" in the investigations in other shootings -- asking for transparency in the investigation of this shooting.
      
    
            Story developing ...

title: Man Jumps Overboard Off Carnival Cruise Ship

Carnival Cruise
                          Man Jumps Overboard, Ship Turns Around to Search
body:
Carnival Cruise
                          Man Jumps Overboard, Ship Turns Around to Search
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 20, 2026
                
                            10:43 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 20, 2026
                                11:48 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A Carnival Cruise ship made a U-turn to search for a man who jumped overboard into the waters off Mexico ... and one of the passengers taking the trip told TMZ all about the tragic event.
      
    
            The search began on Saturday morning as the ship was heading along the coast of Mexico's Baja peninsula.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A rep for Carnival tells TMZ ... "Carnival Cruise Line confirmed Saturday that a male guest aboard Carnival Panorama jumped overboard while the ship was sailing from Puerto Vallarta, Mexico to Long Beach, California."
      

            When they were notified that a guest was missing, the crew reviewed CCTV footage as part of their investigation and alerted both the U.S. and Mexico Coast Guards.
      
    
            The cruise line added ... "Carnival is providing support to the family who was traveling with the guest, and our thoughts and prayers are with them and their loved ones."
      
    
            A passenger tells TMZ ... the incident occurred in the waters along the Baja peninsula as the ship was returning to Long Beach.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The cruise ship guest added ... a family member had guest services page the missing passenger around 10:30 AM after searching for him.
      
    
            After CCTV footage confirmed he went overboard, the ship turned back around at 2 PM to search before resuming its route to Long Beach at approximately 4:30 PM ... the passenger says.
      
    
            We've asked Carnival Cruise Line and the U.S. Coast Guard about the status of the man who jumped overboard ... so far, no word back.
